title: Florida Census Demographics: County and Tract Patterns
text:
Spatial Analysis
The choropleth map reveals a pronounced geographic concentration of Florida’s Hispanic population, primarily clustered in South Florida and the Central Florida I-4 corridor. In South Florida, Miami-Dade County exhibits the highest Hispanic proportion in the state at 68.8%, reflecting historic and continuing immigration from Cuba and across Latin America, while agricultural interior counties like Hendry (57.1%) also sustain majority-Hispanic populations. Central Florida forms a prominent secondary hub centered on Osceola County (56.1%) and Orange County (32.9%), fueled by substantial inward migration of Puerto Rican communities to the Greater Orlando area. In contrast, northern Florida and the Panhandle exhibit significantly lower Hispanic population shares (often below 5%), highlighting a stark regional divergence across the peninsula.

title: About This Project
text:
This project examines county-level demographic patterns across Florida using data from the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2018–2022 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates.

Data & Methodology

Source: U.S. Census Bureau 5-Year American Community Survey via tidycensus
Variables:

Total Population (B01003_001)
Hispanic or Latino Population (B03002_012)
Median Household Income (B19013_001)

Spatial Geometry: Florida county boundary shapefiles via tigris and Census TIGER/Line
Tools: R, tidyverse, sf, ggplot2, and Quarto
